"""ADR-004 bounded revision contracts: terminal rejection, EPS periods, model
version and the judge semantic-validity condition.

The review tests use a Mock store so they assert the state transition itself
(no persistence call, no ledger read) rather than a database implementation.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

import pytest
import yaml

from research_desk.context import build_common_grounding
from research_desk.eval.case_registry import case_for
from research_desk.models import ProposalStatus, utcnow_iso
from research_desk.review import ReviewError, approve, create_proposal, execute, reject


def _proposal(*, price: float = 100.0, proposal_id: str | None = None):
    return create_proposal(
        run_id="run-revision",
        ticker="AAPL",
        trade_date="2026-06-10",
        signal="Buy",
        rating="Buy",
        price=price,
        proposal_id=proposal_id or f"prop-revision-{utcnow_iso()[-9:]}",
    )


def test_rejected_execute_remains_rejected_and_cannot_be_approved():
    """Execution cannot turn a rejection into an approvable REVIEW_REQUIRED row."""
    store = MagicMock()
    proposal = _proposal()
    reject(proposal, operator="leo")
    assert proposal.status == ProposalStatus.REJECTED

    updated, execution = execute(store, proposal, operator="leo")

    assert updated.status == ProposalStatus.REJECTED
    assert execution.executed is False
    assert execution.reason == "proposal rejected"
    store.update_proposal_status.assert_not_called()
    store.apply_transaction.assert_not_called()
    store.get_ledger.assert_not_called()

    with pytest.raises(ReviewError, match="rejected"):
        approve(updated, shares=100, operator="leo")


def test_previously_approved_then_rejected_stays_rejected_on_execute():
    """A rejection is terminal even when an earlier approval version is present."""
    store = MagicMock()
    proposal = _proposal()
    approved = approve(proposal, shares=100, operator="leo")
    assert approved.approved_version
    reject(approved, operator="leo")
    assert approved.status == ProposalStatus.REJECTED

    updated, execution = execute(store, approved, operator="leo")

    assert updated.status == ProposalStatus.REJECTED
    assert execution.executed is False
    assert execution.reason == "proposal rejected"
    store.update_proposal_status.assert_not_called()
    store.apply_transaction.assert_not_called()

    with pytest.raises(ReviewError, match="rejected"):
        approve(updated, shares=100, operator="leo")


def test_common_grounding_names_eps_period_and_ttm_limit():
    grounding = build_common_grounding("AAPL", "2026-07-31", {})
    lower = grounding.lower()
    assert "quarterly eps" in lower
    assert "trailing-twelve-month (ttm)" in lower
    assert "trailing p/e" in lower
    assert "actual ttm evidence" in lower
    # No fixed stock examples or invented figures in the shared rules.
    assert "microsoft" not in lower
    assert "usd90.0b" not in lower


def test_authoritative_model_and_prompt_version_are_consistent():
    from research_desk.config import (
        DEFAULT_BASE_URL,
        DEFAULT_MODEL,
        DEFAULT_PROVIDER,
        PROMPT_VERSION,
        ResearchDeskSettings,
    )
    from research_desk.eval import live

    assert live.MODEL == DEFAULT_MODEL == "deepseek-flash"
    assert live.PROVIDER == DEFAULT_PROVIDER == "deepseek"
    assert DEFAULT_BASE_URL == "https://api.aiohub.org/v1"
    assert ResearchDeskSettings().prompt_version == PROMPT_VERSION

    snapshot = yaml.safe_load(
        Path("prompts/runtime-prompts-v0.1.2.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    )
    assert snapshot["prompt_version"] == PROMPT_VERSION
    assert snapshot["model"] == DEFAULT_MODEL
    assert snapshot["provider"] == DEFAULT_PROVIDER
    assert snapshot["base_url"] == DEFAULT_BASE_URL


def test_judge_prompt_requires_semantic_validity():
    from research_desk.eval.live import _judge_prompt

    prompt = _judge_prompt(
        case_for("AAPL"),
        "report text",
        [],
        available_sources={},
        events=[],
    )
    assert "semantic_valid" in prompt
    assert "semantic_errors" in prompt
    assert "quarterly EPS" in prompt
    assert "trailing P/E" in prompt
    assert "Valid citation IDs do NOT rescue" in prompt


def test_judge_score_defaults_invalid_and_errors_force_false():
    from research_desk.eval.live import JudgeScore

    legacy = JudgeScore(
        support=0.9,
        relevance=0.9,
        cited_claim_count=2,
        supported_cited_claim_count=2,
    )
    assert legacy.semantic_valid is False  # absent field is never a pass
    assert legacy.semantic_errors == []

    flagged = JudgeScore(
        support=0.9,
        relevance=0.9,
        cited_claim_count=2,
        supported_cited_claim_count=2,
        semantic_valid=True,
        semantic_errors=["quarterly EPS labeled as TTM"],
    )
    assert flagged.semantic_valid is False


def test_llm_judge_records_semantic_fields(monkeypatch):
    from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage

    from research_desk.eval import live

    class _FakeLLM:
        def __init__(self):
            self.extra_body = None

        def with_structured_output(self, schema, include_raw=False):
            def invoke(_prompt):
                parsed = live.JudgeScore(
                    support=0.9,
                    relevance=0.9,
                    cited_claim_count=2,
                    supported_cited_claim_count=2,
                    semantic_valid=True,
                    semantic_errors=["quarterly EPS relabeled as TTM"],
                )
                return {"raw": AIMessage(content=""), "parsed": parsed, "parsing_error": None}

            return type("SO", (), {"invoke": staticmethod(invoke)})()

    class _FakeClient:
        def get_llm(self):
            return _FakeLLM()

    monkeypatch.setattr(
        "tradingagents.llm_clients.create_llm_client", lambda *a, **k: _FakeClient()
    )

    _raw, score = live._llm_judge(
        case_for("AAPL"),
        "report text",
        [],
        available_sources={},
        events=[],
    )
    assert score["semantic_valid"] is False
    assert score["semantic_errors"] == ["quarterly EPS relabeled as TTM"]

265: # A monetary number token in ordinary report formatting: optional ``$``/spaces,
266: # an explicit sign, US thousands separators, and a decimal fraction. Ungrouped
267: # integers of any length match, correctly grouped comma amounts match, and the
268: # sign stays part of the numeric value so ``-451.10`` is never read as
269: # ``451.10``. The boundaries reject a digit/comma/dot directly before and a
270: # digit directly after, so the match is never a substring of a larger number
271: # like ``1451.10`` for an expected ``451.10``.
272: _PRICE_TOKEN_RE = re.compile(
273:     r"(?<![\d.,])\$?\s*[+-]?\s*(?:\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})+(?:\.\d+)?|\d+(?:\.\d+)?)(?!\d)"
274: )
275: 
276: 
277: def _normalize_number_token(token: str) -> Decimal | None:
278:     """Parse a matched number token (``$``/commas removed, sign kept) into a Decimal."""
279:     cleaned = token.replace(",", "").replace("$", "").strip()
280:     try:
281:         return Decimal(cleaned)
282:     except InvalidOperation:
283:         return None

286: def _contains_price(text: str, expected_close: float) -> bool:
287:     """True when ``text`` states the expected close as its own number token.
288: 
289:     Ordinary formatting is normalized ($451.10, 451.1, comma thousands, trailing
290:     zeros), so the check accepts exactly the expected numerical value and never
291:     a different number or a substring of a larger number.
292:     """
293:     expected = Decimal(f"{expected_close:.2f}")
294:     for match in _PRICE_TOKEN_RE.finditer(text):
295:         value = _normalize_number_token(match.group(0))
296:         if value is not None and value == expected:
297:             return True
298:     return False

301: def _report_text(final_state: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
302:     """Assemble the material report text a run actually produced.
303: 
304:     Stages keep their authentic upstream role titles (``reporting.py``) so the
305:     independent judge can distinguish intermediate proposals (bull/bear, research
306:     manager, trader, risk analysts) from the final portfolio decision. The
307:     Portfolio Manager node writes the same string to both
308:     ``risk_debate_state.judge_decision`` and ``final_trade_decision``; when they
309:     are exactly equal after whitespace stripping, the identical content is
310:     included once as the final decision. Raw model text is preserved; no
311:     different or contrary stage is removed.
312:     """
313:     parts: list[str] = []
314: 
315:     def _add(title: str, value: Any) -> None:
316:         if isinstance(value, str) and value.strip():
317:             parts.append(f"## {title}\n{value.strip()}")
318: 
319:     for key, title in (
320:         ("market_report", "Market Analyst"),
321:         ("news_report", "News Analyst"),
322:         ("sentiment_report", "Sentiment Analyst"),
323:         ("fundamentals_report", "Fundamentals Analyst"),
324:     ):
325:         _add(title, final_state.get(key))
326: 
327:     debate = final_state.get("investment_debate_state")
328:     if isinstance(debate, dict):
329:         _add("Bull Researcher", debate.get("bull_history"))
330:         _add("Bear Researcher", debate.get("bear_history"))
331:         _add("Research Manager", debate.get("judge_decision"))
332: 
333:     _add("Trader", final_state.get("trader_investment_plan"))
334: 
335:     risk_judge: str | None = None
336:     risk = final_state.get("risk_debate_state")
337:     if isinstance(risk, dict):
338:         _add("Aggressive Analyst", risk.get("aggressive_history"))
339:         _add("Conservative Analyst", risk.get("conservative_history"))
340:         _add("Neutral Analyst", risk.get("neutral_history"))
341:         judge = risk.get("judge_decision")
342:         if isinstance(judge, str) and judge.strip():
343:             risk_judge = judge.strip()
344: 
345:     final = final_state.get("final_trade_decision")
346:     final = final.strip() if isinstance(final, str) and final.strip() else None
347: 
348:     if risk_judge is not None and final is not None and risk_judge == final:
349:         _add("Final Portfolio Decision", final)
350:     else:
351:         _add("Portfolio Manager", risk_judge)
352:         _add("Final Portfolio Decision", final)
353: 
354:     return "\n\n".join(parts)

519: def _observed_tools_text(events) -> str:
520:     """Every actual ``tool_result`` payload in the event log, in event order.
521: 
522:     ``input.data_snapshot`` is a lossy fallback projection keyed by tool
523:     arguments and keeps only the last output for a repeated tool name, so the
524:     judge reads the authoritative event log instead. Each output keeps its
525:     tool/source name and event sequence; an exact duplicate (same tool, same
526:     result) is not repeated, but different results from the same tool survive.
527:     """
528:     lines: list[str] = []
529:     seen: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
530:     for ev in events:
531:         if getattr(ev, "kind", None) != "tool_result":
532:             continue
533:         payload = getattr(ev, "payload", None) or {}
534:         name = payload.get("name") or "unknown"
535:         result = payload.get("result")
536:         if not isinstance(result, str) or not result.strip():
537:             continue
538:         if (name, result) in seen:
539:             continue
540:         seen.add((name, result))
541:         lines.append(f"## observed tool output: {name} (event {getattr(ev, 'seq', '?')})")
542:         lines.append(result)
543:     return "\n".join(lines)

546: def _judge_prompt(
547:     case: dict,
548:     report_text: str,
549:     deterministic: list[dict],
550:     available_sources: dict[str, Any],
551:     events,
552: ) -> str:
553:     """Build the judge prompt from the *actual* frozen evidence captured in this pack.
554: 
555:     Supplies the official earnings notes, the fixed ticker/date/identity and
556:     source IDs, plus the real market evidence (market CSV, verified snapshot and
557:     official news) and every observed tool result recorded in the event log — so
558:     the judge can validate technical/history claims in the report. No
559:     baseline/compact identity is revealed.
560:     """
561:     identity = available_sources.get("identity") or case.get("identity", {})
562:     notes = "\n".join(f"- {n}" for n in case.get("notes", []))
563:     facts = "\n".join(
564:         f"- {c['check']}: {'PASS' if c['passed'] else 'FAIL'} ({c['detail']})"
565:         for c in deterministic
566:     )
567:     market_evidence = str(available_sources.get("market", "")).strip()
568:     verified = str(available_sources.get("verified_snapshot", "")).strip()
569:     news = str(available_sources.get("news", "")).strip()
570:     observed = _observed_tools_text(events).strip()
571: 
572:     return f"""You are an independent equity-research evaluator (a separate role from the analyst). You are judging a single research report for a single equity case. You have no knowledge of which context configuration produced it.
573: 
574: FIXED CASE (identity, do not contest):
575: - ticker: {case['ticker']}
576: - company: {identity.get('company_name', '')}
577: - analysis date: {case['analysis_date']}
578: - source_id: {case.get('source_id', 'n/a')}
579: - official source URL: {case.get('source_url', 'n/a')}
580: 
581: Official earnings notes (frozen source):
582: {notes}
583: 
584: Frozen latest close (from the actual market CSV): {case['latest_close']:.2f}
585: 
586: Market evidence captured in this pack (actual frozen market data this run had available):
587: {market_evidence or '(none present)'}
588: 
589: Verified market snapshot captured in this pack:
590: {verified or '(none present)'}
591: 
592: Company news captured in this pack (official source):
593: {news or '(none present)'}
594: 
595: Observed tool outputs this report's run actually retrieved:
596: {observed or '(none present)'}
597: 
598: Deterministic checks already computed against the report:
599: {facts}
600: 
601: Judge the report below. Score support and relevance on 0-1 using the rubric:
602: - support 1.0 = every key conclusion has direct support from the evidence; 0.8 = main conclusions supported with no key fabrication; 0.5 = important evidence gaps; 0 = key factual fabrication.
603: - relevance 1.0 = fully focused on the requested ticker/date/task; 0.8 = core complete with minor redundancy; 0.5 = missing key parts; 0 = off task.
604: 
605: Citation accounting (count factual claims that carry a source citation):
606: - cited_claim_count = number of factual claims that cite a source ID.
607: - supported_cited_claim_count = number of those cited claims whose cited source ID is present AND actually supports that particular claim. A source ID merely existing is NOT support; it must back the specific claim.
608: - invalid_citation_explanations = for each cited claim whose citation does not support it, explain why.
609: - uncited_factual_claims = factual claims (numbers/dates/identity/price) made with no supporting source ID.
610: Do NOT give 1.0 just because the report is nonempty.
611: 
612: Semantic validity (dedicated condition):
613: - semantic_valid = true only when every earnings-period and unit statement is correct. A quarterly EPS is never described as trailing-twelve-month (TTM) or annual EPS, and a trailing P/E or other trailing ratio is computed only from actual TTM EPS evidence.
614: - Set semantic_valid = false if the report converts or relabels a single-quarter figure as TTM/annual, computes a trailing P/E from quarterly EPS, or makes a key numerical valuation assertion unsupported by the evidence. Valid citation IDs do NOT rescue a wrong period/unit or an unsupported numerical claim.
615: - semantic_errors = concise explanations of each period/unit error or unsupported numerical valuation claim. Any non-empty semantic_errors list must accompany semantic_valid = false.
616: 
617: Presentation contract:
618: - The first section is a deterministic identity/date/evidence-price header rendered from the evidence pack. It is a presentation contract, not model reasoning.
619: - A correct header does NOT excuse a contradictory price or identity in the raw reasoning, nor a wrong earnings period or unit. Judge the generated narrative independently.
620: 
621: REPORT:
622: {report_text}
623: """

626: def _valid_citation_rate(cited: int, supported: int) -> float | None:
627:     """Supported-cited fraction; a zero denominator is NOT an automatic pass."""
628:     if cited <= 0:
629:         return None
630:     return round(supported / cited, 4)

633: class JudgeScore(BaseModel):
634:     """Structured judge output, including the dedicated semantic validity gate.
635: 
636:     ``semantic_valid`` defaults to ``False`` when a legacy or incomplete judge
637:     response omits it, so absence can never be read as a pass. Any recorded
638:     semantic error also forces it to ``False`` regardless of citation counts.
639:     """
640: 
641:     support: float = Field(..., ge=0, le=1)
642:     relevance: float = Field(..., ge=0, le=1)
643:     cited_claim_count: int = Field(..., ge=0)
644:     supported_cited_claim_count: int = Field(..., ge=0)
645:     invalid_citation_explanations: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
646:     uncited_factual_claims: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
647:     semantic_valid: bool = Field(
648:         default=False,
649:         description=(
650:             "True only when earnings periods/units are correct and no key numerical "
651:             "valuation assertion is unsupported by the evidence."
652:         ),
653:     )
654:     semantic_errors: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
655:     rationale: str = ""
656: 
657:     @model_validator(mode="after")
658:     def _supported_within_cited(self):
659:         if self.supported_cited_claim_count > self.cited_claim_count:
660:             raise ValueError(
661:                 "supported_cited_claim_count cannot exceed cited_claim_count"
662:             )
663:         return self
664: 
665:     @model_validator(mode="after")
666:     def _semantic_errors_invalidate(self):
667:         if self.semantic_errors:
668:             self.semantic_valid = False
669:         return self

672: def _llm_judge(
673:     case: dict,
674:     report_text: str,
675:     deterministic: list[dict],
676:     *,
677:     available_sources: dict[str, Any],
678:     events,
679: ):
680:     """Run the real DeepSeek evaluator; returns (raw, score) without fabrication."""
681:     from tradingagents.llm_clients import create_llm_client

683:     client = create_llm_client(
684:         PROVIDER,
685:         MODEL,
686:         base_url=_base_url(),
687:         max_tokens=OUTPUT_CAP,
688:         temperature=0,
689:     )
690:     llm = client.get_llm()
691:     if hasattr(llm, "extra_body"):
692:         llm.extra_body = dict(THINKING_DISABLED_EXTRA_BODY)
693: 
694:     prompt = _judge_prompt(case, report_text, deterministic, available_sources, events)
695:     structured = llm.with_structured_output(JudgeScore, include_raw=True)
696:     try:
697:         raw_out = structured.invoke(prompt)
698:     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - surface judge failures visibly
699:         raw_failed: dict[str, Any] = {"prompt": prompt, "invoke_error": str(exc), "usage": {}}
700:         score: dict[str, Any] = {
701:             "support": None,
702:             "relevance": None,
703:             "cited_claim_count": 0,
704:             "supported_cited_claim_count": 0,
705:             "valid_citation_rate": None,
706:             "invalid_citation_explanations": [],
707:             "uncited_factual_claims": [],
708:             "semantic_valid": False,
709:             "semantic_errors": [],
710:             "rationale": f"judge invoke failed: {exc}",
711:             "error": True,
712:             "deterministic_checks": deterministic,
713:         }
714:         return raw_failed, score
715: 
716:     raw_resp = raw_out.get("raw", None)
717:     parsed = raw_out.get("parsed", None)
718:     parsing_error = raw_out.get("parsing_error", None)
719:     usage: dict[str, Any] = {}

721:         usage = dict(raw_resp.usage_metadata or {}) if raw_resp.usage_metadata else {}
722: 
723:     # Full raw message: tool-call responses often carry content='' with the
724:     # answer in tool_calls, so persist the complete message, not just text.
725:     raw_msg_json: Any = None
726:     if raw_resp is not None:
727:         try:
728:             raw_msg_json = raw_resp.model_dump()
729:         except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
730:             raw_msg_json = {"content": getattr(raw_resp, "content", None)}
731: 
732:     if parsed is None:
733:         score = {
734:             "support": None,
735:             "relevance": None,
736:             "cited_claim_count": 0,
737:             "supported_cited_claim_count": 0,
738:             "valid_citation_rate": None,
739:             "invalid_citation_explanations": [],
740:             "uncited_factual_claims": [],
741:             "semantic_valid": False,
742:             "semantic_errors": [],
743:             "rationale": (
744:                 "judge returned no parseable structured score"
745:                 + (f": {parsing_error}" if parsing_error else "")
746:             ),
747:             "error": True,
748:             "parse_error": str(parsing_error) if parsing_error else None,
749:             "deterministic_checks": deterministic,
750:         }
751:     else:
752:         cited = int(parsed.cited_claim_count)
753:         supported = int(parsed.supported_cited_claim_count)
754:         valid_citation_rate = _valid_citation_rate(cited, supported)
755:         semantic_errors = list(getattr(parsed, "semantic_errors", []) or [])
756:         semantic_valid = bool(getattr(parsed, "semantic_valid", False))
757:         if semantic_errors:
758:             semantic_valid = False  # a recorded semantic defect cannot pass
759:         score = {
760:             "support": float(parsed.support),
761:             "relevance": float(parsed.relevance),
762:             "cited_claim_count": cited,
763:             "supported_cited_claim_count": supported,
764:             "valid_citation_rate": valid_citation_rate,
765:             "invalid_citation_explanations": list(parsed.invalid_citation_explanations),
766:             "uncited_factual_claims": list(parsed.uncited_factual_claims),
767:             "semantic_valid": semantic_valid,
768:             "semantic_errors": semantic_errors,
769:             "rationale": parsed.rationale,
770:             "error": False,
771:             "deterministic_checks": deterministic,
772:         }
773:     raw: dict[str, Any] = {
774:         "prompt": prompt,
775:         "raw_message": raw_msg_json,
776:         "response_text": getattr(raw_resp, "content", None) if raw_resp is not None else None,
777:         "usage": usage,
778:         "parse_error": str(parsing_error) if parsing_error else None,
779:     }

- ``run_judge_case`` uses the real DeepSeek client as an *isolated evaluator*
  (separate role, fixed evidence and rubric, no baseline/compact identity) to
  score a completed run's report, plus deterministic identity/date/price/state
  and source-ID checks. Raw judge response and usage are recorded separately.
- ``run_aggregate`` reads existing output directories and computes six paired
  (baseline vs compact) metrics without calling any model again.

Only host credentials are used: ``DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`` and optional
``DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`` (default ``https://api.aiohub.org/v1``). Each run uses an
isolated home directory. A completed or
failed outcome means the actual graph outcome; a failed setup is never reported
as completed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
import os
import re
import time
from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, model_validator

from ..config import DEFAULT_BASE_URL, DEFAULT_MODEL, DEFAULT_PROVIDER
from .case_registry import case_for
from .frozen_provider import FrozenMarketProvider

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

MODEL = DEFAULT_MODEL
PROVIDER = DEFAULT_PROVIDER
OUTPUT_CAP = 1800  # provider max_tokens cap, identical for both arms
PROVENANCE_FILENAME = "provenance.json"


def _base_url() -> str:
    """Host-supplied endpoint override, otherwise the authoritative default."""
    return os.environ.get("DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL") or DEFAULT_BASE_URL


def _project_root() -> Path:
    """Repository root (this module lives in ``src/research_desk/eval``)."""
    return Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]


def _current_source_fingerprint(root: Path) -> str:
    """Current runtime source fingerprint from the release-quality contract."""
    from .quality import source_fingerprint

    return source_fingerprint(root)


def _provenance_payload(
    fingerprint: str, cfg: dict[str, Any], base_url: str
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Provenance record bound to the actual model/provider/endpoint/config."""
    return {
        "source_fingerprint": fingerprint,
        "model": cfg.get("quick_think_llm") or MODEL,
        "provider": cfg.get("llm_provider") or PROVIDER,
        "endpoint": base_url,
        "deep_think_llm": cfg.get("deep_think_llm") or MODEL,
        "max_tokens": cfg.get("max_tokens"),
        "temperature": cfg.get("temperature"),
    }


def _read_source_fingerprint(path: Path) -> str | None:
    """Read a saved provenance source fingerprint, or None if absent/invalid."""
    try:
        data = json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return None
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        return None
    value = data.get("source_fingerprint")
    return value if isinstance(value, str) else None


# DeepSeek V4 is a thinking model; disable reasoning for a deterministic,
# reproducible research/judge role. Forwarded as ``extra_body`` on the model so
# it reaches the provider request payload.
THINKING_DISABLED_EXTRA_BODY = {"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}}


def _graph_config(home: Path, base_url: str | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Build the evaluation graph config from the real DEFAULT_CONFIG.

    The upstream graph treats the supplied dict as complete, so we start from a
    deep copy of ``DEFAULT_CONFIG`` (which declares ``data_cache_dir``,
    ``results_dir`` and ``memory_log_path``) and then override the explicit
    model/settings. The path fields are pointed inside the arm's isolated home
    so both arms' effective settings are identical and each run stays isolated.
    """
    from copy import deepcopy

    from tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG

    cfg = deepcopy(DEFAULT_CONFIG)
    cfg.update(
        {
            "llm_provider": PROVIDER,
            "quick_think_llm": MODEL,
            "deep_think_llm": MODEL,
            "max_tokens": OUTPUT_CAP,
            "temperature": 0,
            "llm_max_retries": 2,
            "max_debate_rounds": 1,
            "max_risk_discuss_rounds": 1,
            "extra_body": THINKING_DISABLED_EXTRA_BODY,
            "checkpoint_enabled": False,
            "results_dir": str(home / "logs"),
            "data_cache_dir": str(home / "cache"),
            "memory_log_path": str(home / "memory" / "trading_memory.md"),
        }

    return cfg


def _desk_settings(home: Path, max_calls: int | None):
    from research_desk.config import ResearchDeskSettings

    s = ResearchDeskSettings(home=str(home))
    s.analysts = ("market", "news")
    s.max_calls = max_calls
    s.ensure_dirs()
    return s


def _dump_json(path: Path, data: Any) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2, default=str), encoding="utf-8")


def run_evaluate_case(
    ticker: str,
    context_mode: str,
    out_dir: str | Path,
    max_calls: int | None = None,

    """Run one frozen case in one mode; write config/evidence/summary/report."""
    from research_desk.graph_adapter import ResearchRunner
    from research_desk.report import render_run_report

    ticker = ticker.upper()
    if context_mode not in ("baseline", "compact"):
        raise ValueError(f"mode must be baseline|compact, got {context_mode!r}")
    case = case_for(ticker)
    out = Path(out_dir)
    arm_dir = out / ticker / context_mode
    arm_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    if not os.environ.get("DEEPSEEK_API_KEY"):
        raise RuntimeError(
            "DEEPSEEK_API_KEY is not set. Supply it as a host environment variable."
        )

    # graph paths (cache/results/memory) are pointed inside it.
    home = arm_dir / ".home"

        frozen_provider=provider,

    root = _project_root()

    # The pack is exported by the runner under the isolated home; relocate the
    # whole run directory into the arm dir for stable aggregate/export paths.
    run_dir = Path(result.pack_path) if result.pack_path else None

    try:
        pack = EvidencePackIO().import_pack(dest)

    summary = {
        "ticker": ticker,
        "analysis_date": case["analysis_date"],
        "context_mode": context_mode,
        "outcome": result.outcome,
        "signal": result.signal,

        "input_tokens": result.usage.input_tokens,
        "output_tokens": result.usage.output_tokens,
        "total_tokens": result.usage.total_tokens,
        "wall_seconds": round(wall_seconds, 3),
        "error": result.error,
        "pack_complete": pack.complete if pack is not None else False,
        "run_dir": str(dest),

    if pack is not None:
        (arm_dir / "report.md").write_text(render_run_report(pack), encoding="utf-8")

        raise RuntimeError(summary["error"])

def _replace_dir(src: Path, dest: Path) -> None:
    """Move ``src`` to ``dest`` (overwriting any previous dest)."""
    import shutil

    if dest.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(dest)
    dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    shutil.move(str(src), str(dest))

# A monetary number token in ordinary report formatting: optional ``$``/spaces,
# an explicit sign, US thousands separators, and a decimal fraction. Ungrouped
# integers of any length match, correctly grouped comma amounts match, and the
# sign stays part of the numeric value so ``-451.10`` is never read as
# ``451.10``. The boundaries reject a digit/comma/dot directly before and a
# digit directly after, so the match is never a substring of a larger number
# like ``1451.10`` for an expected ``451.10``.
_PRICE_TOKEN_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?<![\d.,])\$?\s*[+-]?\s*(?:\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})+(?:\.\d+)?|\d+(?:\.\d+)?)(?!\d)"
)


def _normalize_number_token(token: str) -> Decimal | None:
    """Parse a matched number token (``$``/commas removed, sign kept) into a Decimal."""
    cleaned = token.replace(",", "").replace("$", "").strip()
    try:
        return Decimal(cleaned)
    except InvalidOperation:
        return None


def _contains_price(text: str, expected_close: float) -> bool:
    """True when ``text`` states the expected close as its own number token.

    Ordinary formatting is normalized ($451.10, 451.1, comma thousands, trailing
    zeros), so the check accepts exactly the expected numerical value and never
    a different number or a substring of a larger number.
    """
    expected = Decimal(f"{expected_close:.2f}")
    for match in _PRICE_TOKEN_RE.finditer(text):
        value = _normalize_number_token(match.group(0))
        if value is not None and value == expected:
            return True
    return False


def _report_text(final_state: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """Assemble the material report text a run actually produced.

    Stages keep their authentic upstream role titles (``reporting.py``) so the
    independent judge can distinguish intermediate proposals (bull/bear, research
    manager, trader, risk analysts) from the final portfolio decision. The
    Portfolio Manager node writes the same string to both
    ``risk_debate_state.judge_decision`` and ``final_trade_decision``; when they
    are exactly equal after whitespace stripping, the identical content is
    included once as the final decision. Raw model text is preserved; no
    different or contrary stage is removed.
    """
    parts: list[str] = []

    def _add(title: str, value: Any) -> None:
        if isinstance(value, str) and value.strip():
            parts.append(f"## {title}\n{value.strip()}")

    for key, title in (
        ("market_report", "Market Analyst"),
        ("news_report", "News Analyst"),
        ("sentiment_report", "Sentiment Analyst"),
        ("fundamentals_report", "Fundamentals Analyst"),
    ):
        _add(title, final_state.get(key))

    debate = final_state.get("investment_debate_state")
    if isinstance(debate, dict):
        _add("Bull Researcher", debate.get("bull_history"))
        _add("Bear Researcher", debate.get("bear_history"))
        _add("Research Manager", debate.get("judge_decision"))

    _add("Trader", final_state.get("trader_investment_plan"))

    risk_judge: str | None = None
    risk = final_state.get("risk_debate_state")
    if isinstance(risk, dict):
        _add("Aggressive Analyst", risk.get("aggressive_history"))
        _add("Conservative Analyst", risk.get("conservative_history"))
        _add("Neutral Analyst", risk.get("neutral_history"))
        judge = risk.get("judge_decision")
        if isinstance(judge, str) and judge.strip():
            risk_judge = judge.strip()

    final = final_state.get("final_trade_decision")
    final = final.strip() if isinstance(final, str) and final.strip() else None

    if risk_judge is not None and final is not None and risk_judge == final:
        _add("Final Portfolio Decision", final)
    else:
        _add("Portfolio Manager", risk_judge)
        _add("Final Portfolio Decision", final)

    return "\n\n".join(parts)


def _report_text_with_identity(pack) -> str:
    """The judge input: the shared deterministic header plus raw generated text."""
    from research_desk.report import render_research_identity

    return render_research_identity(pack) + "\n\n" + _report_text(pack.final_state)


def _deterministic_checks(case: dict, pack, ticker: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Deterministic identity/date/price/state and source-ID checks (QUALITY-001)."""
    checks: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    fs = pack.final_state if pack is not None else {}
    text = _report_text(fs)

    from research_desk.report import render_research_identity

    # Identity/date are presentation-contract checks over the same deterministic
    # header the user-visible report and judge input carry. The raw narrative
    # price check below stays independent and stronger.
    contract_text = render_research_identity(pack) if pack is not None else ""

    def check(name: str, passed: bool, detail: str) -> None:
        checks.append({"check": name, "passed": passed, "detail": detail})

    expected_company = case.get("identity", {}).get("company_name", "")
    check(
        "instrument_identity",
        bool(expected_company) and expected_company.lower() in contract_text.lower(),
        f"report contract references company '{expected_company}'",
    )
    check(
        "analysis_date",
        case["analysis_date"] in contract_text,
        f"report contract references analysis date {case['analysis_date']}",
    )
    check("final_decision_present", bool(fs.get("final_trade_decision")),
          "final trade decision is present in the final state")
    # Price must be supported by evidence (observed tool result or the factual
    # available corpus), never fabricated, AND the report itself must state the
    # expected close. Case metadata alone is not output evidence.
    expected_close = case["latest_close"]
    evidence_supports_price = False
    if pack is not None:
        for bucket in pack.input.data_snapshot.values():
            for res in bucket.values():
                if isinstance(res, str) and _contains_price(res, expected_close):
                    evidence_supports_price = True
        avail = pack.input.available_sources or {}
        for source in (avail.get("market"), avail.get("verified_snapshot")):
            if isinstance(source, str) and _contains_price(source, expected_close):
                evidence_supports_price = True
    reported_price = _contains_price(text, expected_close)
    check(
        "frozen_price_in_report",
        evidence_supports_price and reported_price,
        f"frozen latest close {expected_close:.2f} is supported by evidence and stated in the report",
    )
    source_id = case.get("source_id", "")
    check("source_id_referenced", bool(source_id) and source_id in text,
          f"report references source_id '{source_id}'")
    return checks


def run_judge_case(
    ticker: str,
    out_dir: str | Path,
    max_calls: int | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Judge a completed run's report with a real isolated DeepSeek evaluator.

    Deterministic checks are computed first. Then the real DeepSeek client
    (same model, separate role, fixed evidence and rubric) scores support,
    relevance and citations with a structured rationale. Raw response and usage
    are recorded separately. A score is never auto-assigned for nonempty text.
    """
    from research_desk.evidence import EvidencePackIO

    ticker = ticker.upper()
    if not os.environ.get("DEEPSEEK_API_KEY"):
        raise RuntimeError(
            "DEEPSEEK_API_KEY is not set. Supply it as a host environment variable."
        )
    case = case_for(ticker)
    out = Path(out_dir)
    root = _project_root()
    judged: dict[str, Any] = {"ticker": ticker, "arms": {}}
    source_failure = False
    for mode in ("baseline", "compact"):
        run_dir = out / ticker / mode / "run"
        if not run_dir.exists():
            continue
        current = _current_source_fingerprint(root)
        run_fingerprint = _read_source_fingerprint(
            out / ticker / mode / PROVENANCE_FILENAME
        )
        if run_fingerprint is None:
            judged["arms"][mode] = {
                "error": "run provenance missing; refusing to judge",
            }
            source_failure = True
            continue
        if run_fingerprint != current:
            judged["arms"][mode] = {
                "error": "run provenance is stale; refusing to judge",
                "run_source_fingerprint": run_fingerprint,
                "current_source_fingerprint": current,
            }
            source_failure = True
            continue
        try:
            pack = EvidencePackIO().import_pack(run_dir)
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            logger.warning("cannot import run for %s/%s: %s", ticker, mode, exc)
            judged["arms"][mode] = {"error": str(exc)}
            continue
        if pack.manifest.outcome != "completed" or not pack.final_state:
            judged["arms"][mode] = {
                "outcome": pack.manifest.outcome,
                "note": "skipped judge: run not completed",
            }
            continue
        report_text = _report_text_with_identity(pack)
        deterministic = _deterministic_checks(case, pack, ticker)
        judge_cfg = {
            "llm_provider": PROVIDER,
            "quick_think_llm": MODEL,
            "deep_think_llm": MODEL,
            "max_tokens": OUTPUT_CAP,
            "temperature": 0,
        }
        arm_judge_dir = out / "judge" / ticker / mode
        arm_judge_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        _dump_json(
            arm_judge_dir / PROVENANCE_FILENAME,
            _provenance_payload(current, judge_cfg, _base_url()),
        )
        raw, score = _llm_judge(
            case,
            report_text,
            deterministic,
            available_sources=pack.input.available_sources or {},
            events=pack.events,
        )
        source_after = _current_source_fingerprint(root)
        if source_after != current:
            judged["arms"][mode] = {
                "error": "source changed during judge; refusing to certify",
                "judge_source_fingerprint": current,
                "current_source_fingerprint": source_after,

        judged["arms"][mode] = score

            "source provenance missing or changed; refusing to certify judge results"

def _observed_tools_text(events) -> str:
    """Every actual ``tool_result`` payload in the event log, in event order.

    ``input.data_snapshot`` is a lossy fallback projection keyed by tool
    arguments and keeps only the last output for a repeated tool name, so the
    judge reads the authoritative event log instead. Each output keeps its
    tool/source name and event sequence; an exact duplicate (same tool, same
    result) is not repeated, but different results from the same tool survive.
    """
    lines: list[str] = []
    seen: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
    for ev in events:
        if getattr(ev, "kind", None) != "tool_result":
            continue
        payload = getattr(ev, "payload", None) or {}
        name = payload.get("name") or "unknown"
        result = payload.get("result")
        if not isinstance(result, str) or not result.strip():
            continue
        if (name, result) in seen:
            continue
        seen.add((name, result))
        lines.append(f"## observed tool output: {name} (event {getattr(ev, 'seq', '?')})")

def _valid_citation_rate(cited: int, supported: int) -> float | None:
    """Supported-cited fraction; a zero denominator is NOT an automatic pass."""
    if cited <= 0:
        return None
    return round(supported / cited, 4)


class JudgeScore(BaseModel):
    """Structured judge output, including the dedicated semantic validity gate.

    ``semantic_valid`` defaults to ``False`` when a legacy or incomplete judge
    response omits it, so absence can never be read as a pass. Any recorded
    semantic error also forces it to ``False`` regardless of citation counts.
    """

    support: float = Field(..., ge=0, le=1)
    relevance: float = Field(..., ge=0, le=1)
    cited_claim_count: int = Field(..., ge=0)
    supported_cited_claim_count: int = Field(..., ge=0)
    invalid_citation_explanations: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    uncited_factual_claims: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    semantic_valid: bool = Field(
        default=False,
        description=(
            "True only when earnings periods/units are correct and no key numerical "
            "valuation assertion is unsupported by the evidence."
        ),
    )
    semantic_errors: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    rationale: str = ""

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _supported_within_cited(self):
        if self.supported_cited_claim_count > self.cited_claim_count:

                "supported_cited_claim_count cannot exceed cited_claim_count"
            )

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _semantic_errors_invalidate(self):

    report_text: str,
    deterministic: list[dict],

        PROVIDER,
        MODEL,

            "valid_citation_rate": None,
            "invalid_citation_explanations": [],
            "uncited_factual_claims": [],

    parsed = raw_out.get("parsed", None)

def run_aggregate(root: str | Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Compute six paired baseline/compact metrics from existing run dirs.

    No model is called. Completed arms are included; a missing or non-completed
    arm is recorded as such. Judge scores, when present, are attached separately.
    """
    root = Path(root)
    cases = [c for c in (root.iterdir() if root.exists() else []) if c.is_dir()]
    paired: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for case_dir in sorted(cases):
        ticker = case_dir.name
        arms = {}
        for mode in ("baseline", "compact"):
            summary = case_dir / mode / "summary.json"
            if not summary.exists():
                arms[mode] = {"present": False}
                continue
            data = json.loads(summary.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            data["present"] = True
            judge_file = root / "judge" / ticker / mode / "judge.json"
            if judge_file.exists():
                data["judge"] = json.loads(judge_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            arms[mode] = data
        if not arms.get("baseline", {}).get("present") and not arms.get("compact", {}).get("present"):
            continue
        paired.append({"ticker": ticker, "baseline": arms.get("baseline"), "compact": arms.get("compact")})
    report = _aggregate_report(paired)
    _dump_json(root / "aggregate" / "summary.json", {"paired": paired})
    (root / "aggregate" / "report.md").write_text(report, encoding="utf-8")
    return {"paired": paired, "report": report}


def _arm_value(arm: dict | None, key: str, default=None):
    if arm is None or not arm.get("present"):
        return default
    return arm.get(key, default)


def _aggregate_report(paired: list[dict]) -> str:
    lines = [
        "# Baseline / Compact Aggregate (six paired metrics)",
        "",
        "Read from existing run outputs; no model calls. Judge scores are attached when present.",
        "",
        "| ticker | metric | baseline | compact | delta |",
        "|---|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    metrics = [
        ("calls", "{:.0f}"),
        ("input_tokens", "{:.0f}"),
        ("output_tokens", "{:.0f}"),
        ("total_tokens", "{:.0f}"),
        ("wall_seconds", "{:.1f}"),
        ("outcome", "{!s}"),
    ]
    for p in paired:
        t = p["ticker"]
        for key, fmt in metrics:
            b = _arm_value(p.get("baseline"), key)
            c = _arm_value(p.get("compact"), key)
            b_s = "n/a" if b is None else fmt.format(b)
            c_s = "n/a" if c is None else fmt.format(c)
            delta = "—"
            if isinstance(b, (int, float)) and isinstance(c, (int, float)):
                delta = _pct(b, c)
            lines.append(f"| {t} | {key} | {b_s} | {c_s} | {delta} |")
    for p in paired:
        for mode in ("baseline", "compact"):
            judge = _arm_value(p.get(mode), "judge")
            if isinstance(judge, dict) and not judge.get("error") and judge.get("support") is not None:
                lines.append(
                    f"| {p['ticker']} | {mode} judge support | {judge['support']:.2f} | — | — |"
                )
                lines.append(
                    f"| {p['ticker']} | {mode} judge relevance | {judge['relevance']:.2f} | — | — |"
                )
    return "\n".join(lines)


def _pct(b: float, c: float) -> str:
    if b == 0:
        return "—"
    return f"{(c - b) / b * 100:+.1f}%"

import os
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any
from urllib.parse import urlparse

from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

from .api_key_env import get_api_key_env
from .base_client import BaseLLMClient, normalize_content
from .capabilities import get_capabilities
from .validators import validate_model


class NormalizedChatOpenAI(ChatOpenAI):
    """ChatOpenAI with normalized content output and capability-aware binding.

    The Responses API returns content as a list of typed blocks
    (reasoning, text, etc.). ``invoke`` normalizes to string for
    consistent downstream handling.

    ``with_structured_output`` consults the per-model capability table
    (``capabilities.get_capabilities``) to pick the method and to decide
    whether ``tool_choice`` may be sent. Models that reject ``tool_choice``
    (e.g. DeepSeek V4 and reasoner — per their official tool-calling
    guide) still bind the schema as a tool, but no ``tool_choice``
    parameter is sent.

    Provider-specific quirks beyond structured-output (e.g. DeepSeek's
    reasoning_content roundtrip) live in subclasses so this base class
    stays small.
    """

    def invoke(self, input, config=None, **kwargs):
        return normalize_content(super().invoke(input, config, **kwargs))

    def with_structured_output(self, schema, *, method=None, **kwargs):
        caps = get_capabilities(self.model_name)
        if caps.preferred_structured_method == "none":
            raise NotImplementedError(
                f"{self.model_name} has no structured-output method available; "
                f"agent factories will fall back to free-text generation."
            )
        method = method or caps.preferred_structured_method
        # When the model rejects tool_choice, suppress langchain's hardcoded
        # value. The schema is still bound as a tool — exactly what
        # DeepSeek's official tool-calling examples do.
        if method == "function_calling" and not caps.supports_tool_choice:
            kwargs.setdefault("tool_choice", None)
        return super().with_structured_output(schema, method=method, **kwargs)


class LocalCompatibleChatOpenAI(NormalizedChatOpenAI):
    """OpenAI-compatible client for arbitrary local servers (LM Studio, vLLM,
    llama.cpp via the generic ``openai_compatible`` provider).

    Their tool-calling support varies, and many reject the object-form
    ``tool_choice`` langchain sends for function-calling structured output. Bind
    the schema as a tool but don't force tool_choice, so structured output works
    across local servers regardless of the model ID's capabilities (#1057).
    """

    def with_structured_output(self, schema, *, method=None, **kwargs):
        resolved = method or get_capabilities(self.model_name).preferred_structured_method
        if resolved == "function_calling":
            kwargs.setdefault("tool_choice", None)
        return super().with_structured_output(schema, method=method, **kwargs)


def _input_to_messages(input_: Any) -> list:
    """Normalise a langchain LLM input to a list of message objects.

    Accepts a list of messages, a ``ChatPromptValue`` (from a
    ChatPromptTemplate), or anything else (treated as no messages).
    Used by providers that need to walk the outgoing message history;
    in particular DeepSeek thinking-mode propagation must work for
    both bare-list invocations and ChatPromptTemplate-driven ones, so
    treating only ``list`` here would silently skip half the call sites.
    """
    if isinstance(input_, list):
        return input_
    if hasattr(input_, "to_messages"):
        return input_.to_messages()
    return []


class DeepSeekChatOpenAI(NormalizedChatOpenAI):
    """DeepSeek-specific overrides on top of the OpenAI-compatible client.

    Thinking-mode round-trip is the only DeepSeek-specific behavior that
    stays here. When DeepSeek's thinking models return a response with
    ``reasoning_content``, that field must be echoed back as part of the
    assistant message on the next turn or the API fails with HTTP 400.
    ``_create_chat_result`` captures it on receive and
    ``_get_request_payload`` re-attaches it on send.

    Tool-choice handling for V4 and reasoner — those models reject the
    ``tool_choice`` parameter — is handled by the capability dispatch in
    ``NormalizedChatOpenAI.with_structured_output``, not here.
    """

    def _get_request_payload(self, input_, *, stop=None, **kwargs):
        payload = super()._get_request_payload(input_, stop=stop, **kwargs)
        outgoing = payload.get("messages", [])
        for message_dict, message in zip(outgoing, _input_to_messages(input_), strict=False):
            if not isinstance(message, AIMessage):
                continue
            reasoning = message.additional_kwargs.get("reasoning_content")
            if reasoning is not None:
                message_dict["reasoning_content"] = reasoning
        return payload

    def _create_chat_result(self, response, generation_info=None):
        chat_result = super()._create_chat_result(response, generation_info)
        response_dict = (
            response
            if isinstance(response, dict)
            else response.model_dump(
                exclude={"choices": {"__all__": {"message": {"parsed"}}}}
            )
        )
        for generation, choice in zip(
            chat_result.generations, response_dict.get("choices", []), strict=False
        ):
            reasoning = choice.get("message", {}).get("reasoning_content")
            if reasoning is not None:
                generation.message.additional_kwargs["reasoning_content"] = reasoning
        return chat_result


class MinimaxChatOpenAI(NormalizedChatOpenAI):
    """MiniMax-specific overrides on top of the OpenAI-compatible client.

    M2.x reasoning models embed ``<think>...</think>`` blocks directly in
    ``message.content`` by default, which would pollute saved reports.
    Per platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/text-openai-api,
    ``reasoning_split=True`` redirects the thinking block into
    ``reasoning_details`` so ``content`` stays clean. It is sent via
    ``extra_body`` (not a top-level kwarg) because the openai SDK validates
    top-level params and rejects unknown ones like reasoning_split (#826).

    The flag is gated by ``ModelCapabilities.requires_reasoning_split`` so
    only M2.x reasoning models receive it; non-reasoning MiniMax endpoints
    (Coding Plan, MiniMax-Text-01) never see it.

    Tool-choice handling for M2.x — those models accept only the string
    enum ``{"none", "auto"}`` and reject langchain's function-spec dict —
    is handled by the capability dispatch in
    ``NormalizedChatOpenAI.with_structured_output``, not here.
    """

    def _get_request_payload(self, input_, *, stop=None, **kwargs):
        payload = super()._get_request_payload(input_, stop=stop, **kwargs)
        if get_capabilities(self.model_name).requires_reasoning_split:
            # Pass via extra_body, not as a top-level kwarg: the openai SDK
            # (>=1.56) validates top-level params against Completions.create
            # and rejects unknown ones like reasoning_split (#826). extra_body
            # is forwarded into the request body untouched.
            extra_body = payload.setdefault("extra_body", {})
            extra_body.setdefault("reasoning_split", True)
        return payload


# Kwargs forwarded from user config to ChatOpenAI
_PASSTHROUGH_KWARGS = (
    "timeout", "max_retries", "reasoning_effort", "temperature", "max_tokens",
    "api_key", "callbacks", "http_client", "http_async_client",
)

# OpenAI's ``reasoning_effort`` is only accepted by reasoning models — the GPT-5
# family and the o-series. Non-reasoning models (gpt-4.1, gpt-4o, ...) 400 with
# "Unsupported parameter: 'reasoning.effort' is not supported with this model".
# Drop the kwarg for those rather than crash the run.

def _supports_reasoning_effort(model: str) -> bool:
    """Whether the (native OpenAI) model accepts ``reasoning_effort``."""
    return bool(_OPENAI_REASONING_MODEL.match(model.lower().strip()))


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ProviderSpec:
    """Declarative config for one OpenAI-compatible provider.

    The OpenAI-compatible family (OpenAI, xAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM, MiniMax,
    OpenRouter, Ollama, and any user endpoint) all speak the same Chat
    Completions API and differ only by these fields — so one row here replaces
    the former per-provider base-URL dict, auth handling, and client-class
    branches. Native Anthropic / Google use their own clients (genuinely
    different APIs) and are intentionally NOT in this registry.

    The API-key env var stays in ``api_key_env.PROVIDER_API_KEY_ENV`` (the single
    source consulted by both this client and the CLI prompt); only behavior that
    is provider-specific (base URL, key optionality, wire-format quirks via
    ``chat_class``) lives here.
    """

    chat_class: type = NormalizedChatOpenAI   # provider quirks live in the subclass
    base_url: str | None = None            # default endpoint (None -> SDK default)
    base_url_env: str | None = None        # env var that overrides base_url (e.g. OLLAMA_BASE_URL)
    key_optional: bool = False                # don't require/prompt; send a placeholder if unset
    placeholder_key: str = "EMPTY"            # sent when no key is available (keyless local servers)
    require_base_url: bool = False            # error if no base_url is resolved (generic endpoint)
    use_responses_api: bool = False           # native OpenAI Responses API


# Single source of truth for the OpenAI-compatible provider family. Dual-region
# providers (qwen/glm/minimax) keep separate endpoints because international and
# China accounts cannot share credentials (#758).
OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_PROVIDERS: dict[str, ProviderSpec] = {
    "openai":     ProviderSpec(use_responses_api=True),
    "xai":        ProviderSpec(base_url="https://api.x.ai/v1"),
    "deepseek":   ProviderSpec(base_url="https://api.deepseek.com", chat_class=DeepSeekChatOpenAI),
    "qwen":       ProviderSpec(base_url="https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1"),
    "qwen-cn":    ProviderSpec(base_url="https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1"),
    "glm":        ProviderSpec(base_url="https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4/"),
    "glm-cn":     ProviderSpec(base_url="https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/paas/v4/"),
    "minimax":    ProviderSpec(base_url="https://api.minimax.io/v1", chat_class=MinimaxChatOpenAI),
    "minimax-cn": ProviderSpec(base_url="https://api.minimaxi.com/v1", chat_class=MinimaxChatOpenAI),
    "openrouter": ProviderSpec(base_url="https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"),
    "mistral":    ProviderSpec(base_url="https://api.mistral.ai/v1"),
    "kimi":       ProviderSpec(base_url="https://api.moonshot.ai/v1"),
    "groq":       ProviderSpec(base_url="https://api.groq.com/openai/v1"),
    "nvidia":     ProviderSpec(base_url="https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1"),
    "ollama":     ProviderSpec(base_url="http://localhost:11434/v1", base_url_env="OLLAMA_BASE_URL",
                               key_optional=True, placeholder_key="ollama"),
    # Generic endpoint: user supplies base_url; key optional (keyless local).
    "openai_compatible": ProviderSpec(
        require_base_url=True, key_optional=True, chat_class=LocalCompatibleChatOpenAI
    ),
}


def is_openai_compatible(provider: str) -> bool:
    """Whether ``provider`` is served by the OpenAI-compatible registry."""
    return provider.lower() in OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_PROVIDERS

def _is_native_openai_base_url(base_url: str | None) -> bool:
    """True when ``base_url`` is unset or points at api.openai.com.

    The Responses API (/v1/responses) only exists on native OpenAI. A custom
    base_url on the ``openai`` provider (a proxy, gateway, or local server)
    speaks only Chat Completions, so the Responses API must stay off there even
    though the provider spec enables it (#1024).
    """
    if not base_url:
        return True
    if "://" not in base_url:
        base_url = "https://" + base_url
    host = urlparse(base_url).hostname or ""
    return host == "api.openai.com" or host.endswith(".openai.com")


class OpenAIClient(BaseLLMClient):
    """Client for OpenAI, Ollama, OpenRouter, and xAI providers.

    For native OpenAI models, uses the Responses API (/v1/responses) which
    supports reasoning_effort with function tools across all model families
    (GPT-4.1, GPT-5). Third-party compatible providers (xAI, OpenRouter,
    Ollama) use standard Chat Completions.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        model: str,
        base_url: str | None = None,
        provider: str = "openai",
        **kwargs,
    ):
        super().__init__(model, base_url, **kwargs)
        self.provider = provider.lower()

    def get_llm(self) -> Any:
        """Return a configured ChatOpenAI instance, driven by the provider registry."""
        self.warn_if_unknown_model()
        llm_kwargs = {"model": self.model}
        spec = OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_PROVIDERS.get(self.provider)
        chat_cls = NormalizedChatOpenAI

        if spec is not None:
            chat_cls = spec.chat_class

            # base_url precedence: explicit client base_url (carries the config /
            # TRADINGAGENTS_LLM_BACKEND_URL value) > provider env override (e.g.
            # OLLAMA_BASE_URL) > provider default. None means use the SDK default.
            env_base_url = os.environ.get(spec.base_url_env) if spec.base_url_env else None
            base_url = self.base_url or env_base_url or spec.base_url
            if spec.require_base_url and not base_url:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Provider '{self.provider}' requires a base_url. Set it via "
                    "backend_url / TRADINGAGENTS_LLM_BACKEND_URL to your endpoint, "
                    "e.g. http://localhost:8000/v1 (vLLM) or http://localhost:1234/v1 "
                    "(LM Studio)."
                )
            if base_url:
                llm_kwargs["base_url"] = base_url

            # API key: required unless key_optional; keyless local servers get a
            # placeholder. The env-var name is the single source in api_key_env.
            api_key_env = get_api_key_env(self.provider)
            api_key = os.environ.get(api_key_env) if api_key_env else None
            if api_key:
                llm_kwargs["api_key"] = api_key
            elif spec.key_optional:
                llm_kwargs["api_key"] = spec.placeholder_key
            elif api_key_env:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"API key for provider '{self.provider}' is not set. "
                    f"Please set the {api_key_env} environment variable "
                    f"(e.g. add {api_key_env}=your_key to your .env file)."
                )

            # The Responses API only exists on native OpenAI; if the user points
            # the openai provider at a custom base_url (proxy/gateway/local), it
            # only speaks Chat Completions, so keep Responses off there (#1024).
            if spec.use_responses_api and _is_native_openai_base_url(base_url):
                llm_kwargs["use_responses_api"] = True
        elif self.base_url:
            llm_kwargs["base_url"] = self.base_url

        # Forward user-provided kwargs
        for key in _PASSTHROUGH_KWARGS:
            if key not in self.kwargs:
                continue
            if key == "reasoning_effort" and not _supports_reasoning_effort(self.model):
                continue
            llm_kwargs[key] = self.kwargs[key]

        # The subclass (provider quirks) comes from the registry spec.
        return chat_cls(**llm_kwargs)

    def validate_model(self) -> bool:
        """Validate model for the provider."""
        return validate_model(self.provider, self.model)

from .base_client import BaseLLMClient


def create_llm_client(
    provider: str,
    model: str,
    base_url: str | None = None,
    **kwargs,
) -> BaseLLMClient:
    """Create an LLM client for the specified provider.

    Provider modules are imported lazily so that simply importing this
    factory (e.g. during test collection) does not pull in heavy LLM SDKs
    or fail when their API keys are absent.

    Args:
        provider: LLM provider name
        model: Model name/identifier
        base_url: Optional base URL for API endpoint
        **kwargs: Additional provider-specific arguments

    Returns:
        Configured BaseLLMClient instance

    Raises:
        ValueError: If provider is not supported
    """
    provider_lower = provider.lower()

    # Native (non-OpenAI) APIs are matched first so their string check doesn't
    # import the OpenAI client. Everything else is OpenAI-compatible and routes
    # through the provider registry (single source of truth).
    if provider_lower == "anthropic":
        from .anthropic_client import AnthropicClient
        return AnthropicClient(model, base_url, **kwargs)

    if provider_lower == "google":
        from .google_client import GoogleClient
        return GoogleClient(model, base_url, **kwargs)

    if provider_lower == "azure":
        from .azure_client import AzureOpenAIClient
        return AzureOpenAIClient(model, base_url, **kwargs)

    if provider_lower == "bedrock":
        from .bedrock_client import BedrockClient
        return BedrockClient(model, base_url, **kwargs)

    from .openai_client import OpenAIClient, is_openai_compatible
    if is_openai_compatible(provider_lower):
        return OpenAIClient(model, base_url, provider=provider_lower, **kwargs)

    raise ValueError(f"Unsupported LLM provider: {provider}")

"""Declarative per-model capability table for OpenAI-compatible providers.

This is the single place that knows which model IDs reject which API
parameters or require which structured-output method. The LLM client
subclasses consult ``get_capabilities(model_name)`` instead of hardcoding
model-name ``if`` ladders, so adding a new model (or a new provider quirk)
means editing this table — not the client code.

Pattern adapted from the per-model ``compat:`` flags DeepSeek themselves
publish in their integration guides (e.g. the Oh My Pi config schema
documents ``supportsToolChoice``, ``requiresReasoningContentForToolCalls``
as declarative per-model fields).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Literal

StructuredMethod = Literal[
    "function_calling",  # uses tools; respects supports_tool_choice
    "json_mode",         # uses response_format={"type":"json_object"}
    "json_schema",       # uses response_format={"type":"json_schema",...}
    "none",              # no structured output available; caller falls back to free-text
]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ModelCapabilities:
    """What an OpenAI-compatible model accepts at the API level."""

    supports_tool_choice: bool
    supports_json_mode: bool
    supports_json_schema: bool
    preferred_structured_method: StructuredMethod
    # DeepSeek thinking-mode models 400 if reasoning_content from prior
    # assistant turns is not echoed back on the next request.
    requires_reasoning_content_roundtrip: bool = False
    # MiniMax M2.x reasoning models need ``reasoning_split=True`` so the
    # <think> block lands in ``reasoning_details`` instead of polluting
    # ``content``. The flag is rejected by non-reasoning MiniMax models
    # (Coding Plan, MiniMax-Text-01, etc.), so we only set it where the
    # model actually consumes it. (#826)
    requires_reasoning_split: bool = False


# DeepSeek's thinking models accept the ``tools`` array but reject the
# ``tool_choice`` parameter (official Oh My Pi integration guide and the
# 400 response in issue #678). Their official tool-calling examples
# (api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/tool_calls) pass ``tools=[...]`` without
# ``tool_choice`` — we mirror that pattern by setting supports_tool_choice
# to False and letting the client suppress the kwarg.
_DEEPSEEK_THINKING = ModelCapabilities(
    supports_tool_choice=False,
    supports_json_mode=True,
    supports_json_schema=False,
    preferred_structured_method="function_calling",
    requires_reasoning_content_roundtrip=True,
)

_DEEPSEEK_CHAT = ModelCapabilities(
    supports_tool_choice=True,
    supports_json_mode=True,
    supports_json_schema=False,
    preferred_structured_method="function_calling",
)

# MiniMax M2.x reasoning models accept the tools array, but their
# tool_choice parameter is restricted to the enum {"none", "auto"}
# (platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/text-post). Langchain's
# function_calling path sends tool_choice as a function-spec dict, which
# MiniMax 400s — same shape as the DeepSeek bug. supports_tool_choice=False
# makes the dispatch in NormalizedChatOpenAI suppress the kwarg; the schema
# still ships as a tool. json_mode response_format is only for
# MiniMax-Text-01, not M2.x.
_MINIMAX_THINKING = ModelCapabilities(
    supports_tool_choice=False,
    supports_json_mode=False,
    supports_json_schema=False,
    preferred_structured_method="function_calling",
    requires_reasoning_split=True,
)

_DEFAULT = ModelCapabilities(
    supports_tool_choice=True,
    supports_json_mode=True,
    supports_json_schema=True,
    preferred_structured_method="function_calling",
)


# Exact-ID matches take precedence over pattern matches.
_BY_ID: dict[str, ModelCapabilities] = {
    "deepseek-chat": _DEEPSEEK_CHAT,
    "deepseek-reasoner": _DEEPSEEK_THINKING,
    "deepseek-v4-flash": _DEEPSEEK_THINKING,
    "deepseek-v4-pro": _DEEPSEEK_THINKING,
    # MiniMax — full official model lineup per
    # platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/text-openai-api
    "MiniMax-M2.7": _MINIMAX_THINKING,
    "MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed": _MINIMAX_THINKING,
    "MiniMax-M2.5": _MINIMAX_THINKING,
    "MiniMax-M2.5-highspeed": _MINIMAX_THINKING,
    "MiniMax-M2.1": _MINIMAX_THINKING,
    "MiniMax-M2.1-highspeed": _MINIMAX_THINKING,
    "MiniMax-M2": _MINIMAX_THINKING,
}

# Forward-compat patterns. New ``deepseek-v5-*`` / ``deepseek-reasoner-*``
# or ``MiniMax-M3*`` variants inherit the thinking-mode quirks automatically.
_BY_PATTERN: list[tuple[re.Pattern[str], ModelCapabilities]] = [
    (re.compile(r"^deepseek-v\d"), _DEEPSEEK_THINKING),
    (re.compile(r"^deepseek-reasoner"), _DEEPSEEK_THINKING),
    (re.compile(r"^MiniMax-M\d"), _MINIMAX_THINKING),
]


def get_capabilities(model_name: str) -> ModelCapabilities:
    """Resolve capabilities by exact ID, then pattern, then default."""
    # OpenRouter namespaces official DeepSeek models as ``deepseek/<id>``, so
